record.original_question: Can the positive integers be partitioned into infinitely many arbitrary classes in such a way that at least one class contains an arithmetic progression of R terms for some fixed R > 3, and what is the largest value of R for which this is always possible?

evidence.quote: Is it possible to partition N* into an infinity of arbitrary classes such that at least one class contain an arithmetic progression of R terms (R> 3)? Find a maximum R having this property.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N}^* = \{1, 2, 3, \dots\}$ denote the set of positive integers. Consider partitions of $\mathbb{N}^*$ into infinitely many nonempty classes $\{C_i\}_{i \in I}$ (with $|I| = \aleph_0$), where the partition is otherwise arbitrary.

Determine the largest integer $R > 3$ (if any exists) with the following property: for every such partition of $\mathbb{N}^*$ into infinitely many classes, at least one of the classes $C_i$ contains an arithmetic progression of length $R$, i.e., $R$ distinct integers $a, a+d, a+2d, \dots, a+(R-1)d$ all belonging to a common class.

Equivalently, decide whether such an integer $R$ exists, and if so identify its maximum value.
artifact.category_tag: Ramsey theory / van der Waerden-type partitions
artifact.status_search_result: Searches on related Smarandache-type partition problems concerning arithmetic progressions return general results (e.g., that any partition of a set containing an infinite arithmetic progression into two pieces yields one piece with infinitely many 3-term APs), but no source was found that resolves the specific question of the largest R > 3 forced when partitioning N* into infinitely many arbitrary classes. The status appears unresolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Partition of a Set Which Contains an Infinite Arithmetic (Respectively Geometric) Progression
status_evidence.snippet: For any partition of a set which contains an infinite arithmetic progression into two disjoint subsets, at least one of these subsets contains an infinite number of triplets in AP.
status_evidence.claim: Related Smarandache-type partition results address only 2-class partitions and 3-term APs, not the infinite-class case for larger R.

status_evidence.title: Finite and infinite arithmetic progressions in sumsets
status_evidence.snippet: Results on arithmetic progressions in sumsets, unrelated to the specific question about infinite-class partitions.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the specific maximum-R question was located.
